book.title: The New Penguin Book of The Guardian Crosswords, volume 7

clue.text: Bird with sadly trite morning song whose mate lost his head

indicators.note: something sadly treated is left in a sorry, disordered state, so the letters beside it are rearranged

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
these five letters rearranged
a.m. marks the morning hours
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A dawn chorus bird sings a dull, clichéd song.
explanation.walkthrough: Henrietta Maria was the queen of Charles I of England, who was beheaded in 1649; the definition is the closing relative clause.
explanation.definitionFit: Her husband King Charles I was executed by beheading, so she is literally the woman whose spouse lost his head.

clue.text: See 9
Bird goes round in roll

indicators.note: goes ... in says one item travels inside the other, here the ring-shaped letter inside the list

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bird spins round and round in a roll of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is the male domestic fowl, the cock, a kind of farmyard bird.

clue.text: Sailors in appropriate cover find beastly saint

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second, the cover wrapped around it

parts.note: a beard is the cover fitting a man's chin
RN is the Royal Navy, its sailors

explanation.surface: Naval men under suitable shelter come across a saint who is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like an insult, but the saint is a beast: the St Bernard is a large mountain-rescue dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A St Bernard is a breed of dog, so the saint named Bernard is literally an animal, a beast.

clue.text: Truck for getting food to mouth?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an industrial vehicle with prongs for raising loads
second meaning, read literally: raising something with the eating implement

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, splitting the vehicle's name into the table tool and the act of raising.
explanation.definitionFit: The warehouse vehicle is named for its prongs, and a diner raising food on a prong performs the same action.

clue.text: Put films on reel before driver?

parts.note: to reel in a line is to wind it
to screen is to show films

explanation.surface: A projectionist threads film onto a reel before the showing.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' means coming after, so the showing follows the reeling. 'Before' then belongs to the definition, meaning in front of.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass pane of a car sits directly in front of the person at the wheel.

clue.text: Look at Georgian city taking preparation for ball

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
Bath is an English city famous for its Georgian architecture

explanation.surface: Someone admires a Georgian city while getting ready for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball is not a dance but the eyeball; Bath is a spa city in Somerset, England, built largely in the Georgian era.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebath is a small cup holding a lotion used to rinse and soothe the eyeball.

clue.text: Churchman is quiet on row

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
taken as written
a tiff is a minor quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A clergyman stays silent about an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiff is a title of the Pope or a bishop, a senior figure in the Church.

clue.text: Boxer's blow makes one extremely angry

parts.note: right is an old intensifier, as in right good, meaning very
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: A punch in the ring leaves someone furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A right cross is a punch thrown with the right hand across the body, a standard boxing shot.

clue.text: Members people initially start to stop

parts.note: arms are limbs, members of the body
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Club members urge people to set something going and then halt it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wry: nations begin stockpiling weapons supposedly to deter, that is to stop, an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitive weapons build-ups are begun as deterrence, a buildup meant to prevent war, and then everyone wants them halted.

clue.text: Note gives authority for capital punishment

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
to allow is to authorise

explanation.surface: A written memo authorises an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: The gallows is the frame for hanging, standing by metonymy for the death penalty itself.

clue.text: Dog on a hill needs keeper

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A dog out on a hillside needs someone to look after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the person in charge of a museum or collection, its custodian.

clue.text: Procedure for making a hole in cloth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a routine practised, as in a fire exercise
third meaning: a strong twilled cotton fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction for punching through fabric, but it is three separate meanings of the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a rehearsed routine, a boring tool, and a hard-wearing twilled cotton fabric.

clue.text: Decoration without toppin' for cake used as drug

indicators.note: the dropped final g of this word is a model, showing the clipped ending wanted for the cake covering
without in its old sense means outside, so the decoration goes around the other part

parts.note: a medal is a military decoration
icing tops a cake, and here loses its final letter like the clue's own spelling

explanation.surface: A cake decoration without its top layer is used as a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in toppin' is the hint: the cake topping, icing, must be dropped-g in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal describes a substance having healing properties, one employed as a remedy or medicine.

clue.text: Those who loot, if the French boat gets publicity in there

indicators.note: in there means everything listed before goes inside the final word

parts.note: the first four letters of the outer word
taken as written
le is French for the
a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
an ad is an advertisement
the outer word's last letter

explanation.surface: Looters board a French vessel and are in the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rifle Brigade was a British Army regiment; the definition puns on rifle as a verb, to ransack.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search and steal, so a brigade of riflers is jokingly a band of plunderers.

clue.text: In former time the Guardian's proceeding as it should

indicators.note: in places the newspaper's possessive inside the phrase for an earlier time

parts.note: once means at some former time
the newspaper speaking of itself says ours

explanation.surface: Once, this newspaper's affairs ran smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the setter's own paper, so its possessive is ours.
explanation.definitionFit: On course is an idiom meaning on track to reach a goal, progressing as planned.

clue.text: See 13
Sea-urchin's relation has first option

indicators.note: an option is an alternative, so the words are taken in an alternative arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea creature's relative gets first choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish and sea urchins are both echinoderms, spiny-skinned marine animals of one phylum, so they are kin.

clue.text: Where lawyers lie with wounding words?

definitions.note: describes remarks; barbed is an adjective for hurtful speech

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
with the preceding Where, the place one lies down is a bed

explanation.surface: A cynical question about where lawyers tell their untruths, using cutting language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' hints at lawyers telling fibs, but it means reclining.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbed remarks are sharply hurtful, pointed like a hook's barb that tears on the way out.

clue.text: Sam's nephew has the last word about his costa

indicators.note: about means around, so the closing word wraps the other part

parts.note: amen ends a prayer
the word paired with Costa in the name of the country between Nicaragua and Panama

explanation.surface: A man's nephew has the final say about his holiday coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam is Uncle Sam, the personification of the USA, and his costa is the Rica that goes with Costa.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam personifies the United States, so any citizen is figuratively his nephew.

clue.text: Cricketer's line calling for the press?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the white line marking where the batsman stands
second meaning: a fold in cloth that needs ironing out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricketer giving a quote to journalists; the press is in fact an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it is the marked line at the wicket; in clothing it is a wrinkle that an iron removes.

clue.text: Invariable instruction for half-standard: rue result

indicators.note: a result is something produced from the given material, here letters remade into a new phrase

parts.note: all fifteen letters used

explanation.surface: A flag at half mast prompts an order to regret the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard and fast rule is a strict regulation admitting no exceptions, a fixed directive.

clue.text: A hut wrecked at airport in literary style

definitions.note: adverbial phrase for an adjective; reads as written in a writer's manner

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so its letters come out in a different order

parts.note: these three letters rearranged
Orly is a Paris airport

explanation.surface: A shack destroyed at an airport, described with literary flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorly means characteristic of a writer, so it describes prose done in a bookish manner.

clue.text: Conclusion of address after ethical statement

parts.note: post- means after, as in postwar
a code of conduct sets out ethical rules

explanation.surface: A speech ends after a statement of principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is a postal address.
explanation.definitionFit: The postcode is the alphanumeric code written last on a British postal address.

clue.text: Annoying trait in royal revolutionary

definitions.note: irritant is used as an adjective here

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning the existing order, so the letters are turned upside down into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A tiresome quirk shows up in a royal who is a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant substance or person causes irritation, so it is irritating, vexing.

clue.text: Citizen, one of the good and great, has socialist party in trap

definitions.text: Citizen, one of the good and great

indicators.note: in places the party inside the snare

parts.note: a gin is a snare for animals
the ILP was Britain's Independent Labour Party

explanation.surface: A worthy member of society has a left-wing group caught in a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gilpin is the hero of Cowper's comic poem, which opens: John Gilpin was a citizen of credit and renown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper presents his linen draper as a respectable Londoner of credit and renown, a notable townsman.

clue.text: Birds hesitantly get up and start again

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Birds rise uncertainly and set off once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to carry on after a pause, beginning a task anew.

clue.text: See 22
